subject: Interactive vs Batch Token Profile — SLO alignment & next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@brightlane.ai>, BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 20:03:00 GMT
Subject: Interactive vs Batch Token Profile — SLO alignment & next steps

Hi Emily / BrightLane team — thanks for the call earlier. Quick post-call recap and the concrete asks so we can size a pilot: 

Summary of what we heard (high level)
- Primary usage: interactive customer support chat (short bursts, 2–10 user messages) + nightly batch enrichment that annotates up to 3M documents per day.
- Typical interactive session: 1–6 messages, average 400 tokens per user turn; tokens generated by model ~350 tokens per reply.
- Nightly batch: high sustained token throughput for 2–3 hours (bulk transforms), with occasional tighter bursts when backfills run.

Performance expectations / SLOs (what you said)
- Client SLO: P95 first-token latency <= 250 ms (interactive), P95 end-to-end <= 800 ms for complete reply.
- Throughput: steady-state interactive QPS ~40 (concurrent sessions ~30), peak crest during campaigns ~300 QPS for 30–60s windows.
- Batch: sustained token rate target ~12k tokens/sec during nightly job windows; peaks up to ~18k tokens/sec for short spikes.

Our initial sizing notes (rough) — please treat as draft
- Interactive path (low-latency): ~30 concurrent streaming sessions; assume 1.2k tokens/sec aggregate during normal day windows across those sessions.
- Peak campaign headroom: plan for 3–4x transient QPS multiplier (target reserve to handle 300 QPS short crests).
- Batch path: recommend reserved capacity that can sustain 12k tokens/sec with autoscale headroom to 18k for 5–10 minute spikes.

Attachments: throughput_estimates.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB) with per-path micro-sim scenarios and the sample_stream_playback.jsonl we discussed.

Asks / next steps
1) Emily: please send a 2-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized stream/playback) and one representative nightly batch job log. The sample_stream_playback.jsonl attachment is an example of how to format it.
2) BrightLane Ops: confirm whether the batch window is elastic (can be shifted) or fixed to midnight. If flexible, a staggered approach reduces peak headroom needed.
3) Redwood action: we’ll run two quick sims: (A) interactive-only sizing to meet P95 first-token <=250ms and (B) combined interactive+batch with conservative mixing to show required reserved units. Expect simulation outputs & a recommendation by EOD tomorrow PST.

I’ll also loop Marissa (ops lead) to propose an initial pilot config (small dedicated pool + autoscale rules).

Thanks — Avery
--

Thanks Avery — that recap is great and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side:

- Interactive: our current weekday peak is closer to 60 concurrent sessions (not 30) during product release windows; normal is ~30. The 300 QPS crest is accurate during marketing pushes, usually lasts 20–45s.
- Batch: nightly job is currently fixed at 02:00 local time but Ops is ok to discuss shifting by up to 2 hours if it eases capacity constraints elsewhere.

We can provide the anonymized 2-hour playback (will scrub PII) and a 1-hour slice of the nightly job logs. Expect those in a secure link by tomorrow morning PST.

One ask: when you run the sims, can you include both a quantized model profile (8-bit) and a fp16 profile so we can compare cost vs latency tradeoffs?

I'll send the playback link shortly.

—Emily

emily@brightlane.ai

Avery / Jonas — forwarding BrightLane response. Quick internal note:

- If they actually hit 60 concurrent interactive sessions during peaks, we should size interactive pool to meet P95 first-token <=250ms with a 1.5x buffer; that suggests reserving ~1.5–2k tokens/sec of low-latency capacity for interactive.
- For batch, prioritizing fp16 will likely reduce GPU count but may push 95th latency for long sequences; recommend we present both cost/lateny curves as Emily requested.
- Pilot proposal (minimum viable): 1 dedicated low-latency node group (pinned to interactive model variant) + 1 reserved batch fleet with autoscale to handle short spikes. Keep canary routing so interactive can fall back to slightly lower-quality variants if load exceeds thresholds.

Jonas: can you sketch a draft pilot config (node sizes, autoscale thresholds, expected monthly burn estimate) by 10:30 PST? I'll review and then we'll send to BrightLane alongside our sims.

Marissa

Perfect — thanks Emily and team. Next steps and schedule: 

1) BrightLane: share the two artefacts (2-hour playback + 1-hour batch slice) via the secure link today.
2) Redwood (Marissa / Jonas / Avery): run sims for both fp16 and 8-bit quantized profiles, plus an interactive-only and combined profile. Deliverable: sizing table (nodes, reserved tokens/sec, buffers), cost estimate, and short notes on fallback policies. Delivery target: EOD tomorrow PST.
3) Pilot kickoff: tentatively target Wed 2028-01-24 for a 48-hour pilot window. We’ll need an ops contact for live monitoring during the pilot — tagging BrightLane Ops in case they can provide a pager rotation.

If that timeline looks good, we’ll send a short Miro/Runbook for the pilot and a DocuSign cover letter for the pilot terms (no long-term commitment).

Thanks again — looking forward to the sample link.
